note: [agent-bulk] Small event, 8 segments; vertex judged from the event's own +-137.9 cm sweep (event_half_span_cm 137.9, under the 150 cm trigger, so no --vtx-span re-capture) and from the two shower frames, in both of which the star and the shower X coincide at the apex of a clear V. Vertex is GOOD: four segments have dvtx 0.0, all cluster 5 -- 5025 (pdg 13, 125.2 cm muon), 5015 (pdg 211, 50.6 cm), 5006 (pdg 211, 2.7 cm stub) and the shower seed 5026 (pdg 11, 9.2 cm) -- a proper multi-prong numu CC vertex, and the three non-EM prongs are correctly left UNOWNED. VERDICT on 5026 (112.4 MeV, 3 segments) is correct. NOTHING IS MISSING: the only two non-members in the event are 23020 (3.0 MeV) at 29.0 cm / 87.6 deg and 25022 (1.4 MeV) at 68.1 cm / 40.8 deg, both well outside the cone; there is no grey charge contiguous with the member set inside the cone at any distance. A DENSITY READING I CHECKED AND THEN WITHDREW, worth recording because it nearly produced a wrong flag: 112.4 MeV over a 9.2 cm skeleton is 12 MeV/cm, which would be far above MIP and would have read as a proton. But in the 3-D view at az-055 the point spray above the X extends roughly three times further than the skeletonised segment (about 30 cm against 9 cm), so the charge is spread over the spray and the real density is about 3.7 MeV/cm -- shower-like. The lesson is that kine_charge is blob charge and the table's `length` is skeleton length, and dividing one by the other overstates density whenever the skeleton under-covers the blob. I flag it here because I used the same MeV/cm argument on evt53658 and evt105074 in this shard, and on those two it was supported by the 3-D picture (a straight uniform narrow line), whereas here it is not. STUB TRAIL, described not verdicted: the other two members are 22019 (pdg 13, 2 points, 41.3 cm / 15.0 deg) and 24021 (pdg 13, 2 points, 76.8 cm / 23.6 deg), both absorbed by pass3_cone. 76.8 cm is 5.5 X0 for a 112 MeV shower, which is not credible as shower tail, so I think 24021 at least does not belong -- but both are 2-point specks whose charge is negligible against 112.4 MeV, so removing them would not move the energy and I did not mark them or downgrade the verdict on their account. Note the ANGLE-MONOTONICITY point that recurs across my shard: this shower accepted at 23.6 deg / 77 cm while other showers in the same sample reject at 6 deg / 47 cm. VERTEX ATTACHMENT: 5026's start is at dist 0.0 from the vertex in a numucc_em event, so it cannot be a converted photon -- it is prompt EM activity at the vertex (or a photon that converted immediately). That is an observation, not a verdict, and unlike evt98844 nothing here rests on it. NOT looked at: 23020 (3.0 MeV) and 25022 (1.4 MeV), the only other showers. No pi0: no reco group, pio slots None, only one shower above 20 MeV in the event so no pairing is possible and I propose none. drag_check live: probe_radius_px 69.8, seg_u 49.83 -> 20.62, cloud_u -18.34 -> -12.44, cloud_redrew true, probe_degenerate false.
